A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RainPro-8 and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-J. Matching content across layout changes and renumbering supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original European precipitation forecasting and SEVIR experiments, ablations, input attribution and repeated-run results (Section 4; Appendices C and G).

after.justification: v3 retains original RainPro-8 and RainPro-2R experimental outcomes, including benchmark scores, ablations, attribution and repeated-run results.

M1.justification: The ordinal-consistent loss, exponential lead-time weighting, single-pass U-Net/MaxViT architecture and RainPro-2R adaptation remain unchanged (Section 3; Appendix H). Edits clarify wording and equation presentation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate European multisource forecasting over eight hours and radar-only SEVIR nowcasting. Data sources, geographic coverage and test scenarios in Appendices A, D and H are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MetNet-3*, GFS, PySTEPS, Earthformer, SimVP and the radar-only RainPro variant. The comparator sets in the ablation table, SEVIR table and DiffCast comparison also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Training budgets, hyperparameters, splits, sample counts, preprocessing and evaluation metrics are retained. Appendix H preserves the same SEVIR protocol: five input frames, twenty predicted frames, 128-by-128 resolution and 200,000 training iterations.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same loss, lead-time conditioning, weighting and radar-only ablations. Integrated Gradients analyses, three forecast case studies and the robustness analysis in Appendices C, D and G are unchanged; rearranged maps add no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state that primary experiments use one training run and report means and standard deviations from three independent runs for RainPro-8 and its cross-entropy variant (Appendix G, Table 10). Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported scores, timings, rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains RainPro-8 CSI 0.279 and FSS 0.537, and Table 3 retains RainPro-2R CSI 0.3524. Figures 2 and 4 redisplay existing results.

T1.justification: The probability derivations, loss definitions and metric formulas are unchanged. v2's combined Equation 7 is displayed as Equations 7-9 in v3, shifting subsequent numbering without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The rewritten contribution bullets preserve the claims of efficient multisource forecasting, simultaneous lead-time prediction, superiority over existing methods and SEVIR versatility. The abstract and conclusion retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of data-source importance, ordinal-loss benefits and the tradeoff between perceptual sharpness and pixelwise accuracy. Future work still identifies missing-input robustness and automatic threshold learning (Sections 4-5).

D1.justification: v2 contains a code URL placeholder and promises future release; v3 supplies the rafapablos/RainPro repository address and reports public availability with data-access instructions. New acknowledgments identify Lambda and GenomeDK as compute providers. Detailed implementation and hardware specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged. Explicitly naming MetNet-3 beside its existing citation in Section 3.4 clarifies wording without changing attribution or research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the three contribution bullets and makes limited prose refinements. It adds acknowledgments, updates author/header text and removes the reproducibility statement's section number, while preserving the broader narrative and section sequence.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes from three plots in one row to a two-row arrangement with a relocated legend. Figure 4 changes from eight maps in one row to a two-by-four arrangement with revised labels and colorbar ticks. Equations and table placement also change, while appendix displays remain unchanged apart from headers and numbering.

improvement.justification: v3 replaces the code placeholder and release promise with concrete access information, and improves the readability of Figures 2 and 4 and the lead-time equations. These provide limited gains in reproducibility documentation and presentation; the scientific method, experimental evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
